# Deploying Models with Streamlit

## Overview
A model sitting in a notebook helps no one; deployment is how you put it in front of users so it delivers value, and Streamlit is the fastest way for a data scientist to do this without web development experience. The workflow is: train your model, save it to a file with joblib or pickle, then write a Streamlit app, a plain Python script where simple commands like st.slider, st.selectbox, and st.write create an interactive web interface. Your app loads the saved model, collects input from the user through widgets, runs a prediction, and displays the result, all in a browser. Because it's pure Python, you can go from model to working web app in an afternoon. Once it works locally, you can deploy it to Streamlit Community Cloud for free by connecting your GitHub repository, giving you a public URL to share. This is a transformative skill for beginners: it lets you build tangible, shareable data products (a price predictor, a churn calculator, a recommendation demo) that impress employers far more than a static notebook.

## Deep Dive
This module covers: Why deployment matters; Saving and loading models (joblib/pickle); Building a Streamlit app; Accepting user input and showing predictions; Deploying to Streamlit Community Cloud. Mastering these ideas is essential because they appear repeatedly in production AI systems.

### What You Will Learn
- The core theory behind today's topic.
- How to apply it using Python, NumPy, Pandas, or the relevant framework.
- How to evaluate results and avoid common mistakes.
- Where to find authoritative references when you need deeper detail.

### Real-World Context
In industry, these skills are used daily: data scientists clean messy survey data, AI engineers deploy models to REST APIs, and automation engineers orchestrate pipelines. Today's practical task simulates one of these real-world scenarios.

## Hands-On Practice
**Practical Task:** Save a trained model, build a Streamlit app that takes user inputs through widgets, loads the model, and displays a live prediction, then run it locally.
**Mini Project:** Deploy one of your models as a public Streamlit app: build the interface, connect it to your saved model, push it to GitHub, and deploy it to Streamlit Community Cloud with a shareable link.
**Assignment:** Add input validation and a clear explanation of the prediction to your Streamlit app so a non-technical user understands the result.

Complete all three sections. Each completed section earns points toward your CalibiAI Score. If you are unsure about any part, use the AI assessment popup to submit your work and receive dynamic feedback from DeepSeek.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid
Many beginners rush into coding before fully understanding the data. Others skip validation steps and overestimate model performance. This module helps you build the discipline of checking assumptions first, then applying algorithms systematically.

## Career Impact
The skills covered today are frequently tested in technical interviews and required in entry-level AI engineering roles. Building a portfolio that demonstrates mastery of these concepts will significantly improve your job prospects.

## Key Takeaways
1. Theory guides practice — understand before coding.
2. Clean data and clear metrics are more valuable than complex models.
3. Document your steps for reproducibility.
4. Communication matters: explain results to non-technical stakeholders.

- Check the GitHub repositories for working code examples.
